english: a friend in need is a friend indeed

terms.latin: Is est amīcus quī in rē dubiā rē juvat.
evidence: Plaut. Epid. 113: is est amīcus, quī in rē dubiā rē juvat, ubi rēst opus
terms.comment: Literally “he is a friend who helps in deed in a doubtful matter”. A line of Plautus; Traupman drops its end, ubi rēst opus, “when there is need of it”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Plautus, Epidicus 113, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (12 November 2026).
